title: LLM-Powered Automatic Translation and Urgency in Crisis Scenarios
abstract: arXiv:2602.13452v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for crisis preparedness and response, particularly for multilingual communication. However, their suitability for high-stakes crisis contexts remains insufficiently evaluated. This work examines the performance of state-of-the-art LLMs and machine translation systems in crisis-domain translation, with a focus on preserving urgency, a critical property for effective crisis communication and triage. Using multilingual crisis data (TICO-19, 30 languages) and a newly introduced urgency-annotated dataset of 100 scenarios translated into 29 languages, we show that dedicated translation models and LLMs exhibit substantial quality degradation, particularly for low-resource languages. translated_title: 基于大语言模型的危机场景自动翻译与紧迫性处理
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地被提出用于危机准备和响应，特别是在多语言通信方面。然而，它们在高风险危机情境中的适用性仍未得到充分评估。本研究考察了最先进的LLMs和机器翻译系统在危机领域翻译中的性能，重点关注紧迫性的保留——这是有效危机沟通和分诊的关键属性。利用多语言危机数据（TICO-19，30种语言）以及一个新引入的、包含100个场景并翻译成29种语言的紧迫性标注数据集，我们发现专用翻译模型和LLMs表现出显著的质量下降，尤其是在低资源语言中。除了翻译质量外，我们进行了一项人工标注研究，揭示了一个显著的不对称性：人类评估者无论提示语言如何，都保持一致的紧迫性判断，而基于LLM的评估则表现出不一致性。
tldr: 本研究揭示了LLMs和翻译系统在危机场景翻译中质量下降，尤其在低资源语言中，且LLM在紧迫性判断上存在不一致性，而人类评估则保持一致。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that LLMs and translation systems degrade in crisis-domain translation, especially for low-resource languages, and LLM-based urgency judgments are inconsistent, unlike human assessors.
